questions.q: A customer calls from a phone number and you don't know whether it belongs to an Account, Contact, or Lead. Which tool fits?
options: SOQL, with a separate query per object and no other option
SOQL with GROUP BY
Neither; Salesforce cannot search phone numbers
SOSL, searching phone fields across all three objects in one statement
questions.explain: SOSL is built for finding text when you don't know which object holds it, and it can search several objects at once.

questions.q: You need the total Opportunity Amount by owner. Which tool?
options: SOSL, using FIND {Amount}
SOQL, using SUM and GROUP BY
Either one; both support aggregates
SOSL, using RETURNING Opportunity
questions.explain: Aggregates like SUM, COUNT and GROUP BY are SOQL features. SOSL has none.

questions.q: Which is a real difference in result size between the two?
options: Both return exactly 2,000 records always
SOSL returns up to 2,000 records in total; SOQL can retrieve large result sets in batches
Neither has any limits
SOQL is limited to 2,000 records and SOSL is unlimited
questions.explain: SOSL caps results at 2,000 records, which makes it a poor choice for bulk extraction. SOQL results can be fetched in batches.

questions.q: Which task is best suited to SOQL?
options: Export every Contact created this year
Find any record mentioning the word 'renewal'
Rank results by how well they match a search term
Find which object contains a given email address
questions.explain: One known object, a date condition, and a large result set: that is a structured SOQL query.

questions.q: How are SOSL results organized, compared with SOQL?
options: Grouped by object and ranked by relevance, rather than sorted by fields you choose
As nested parent-to-child lists
As a single flat table with every object combined
Identically to SOQL results
questions.explain: SOSL returns matching records grouped by object, ordered by relevance to the search term.
